metadata.title: Brieffragment von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.109a

context:
## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brieffragment von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.109a
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.109a
- Datum: 04.1941
- Objekttyp: Brieffragment
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
3
We changed over quickly to Sch.'s as the headmistress of the school
in New Rochelle had suggested a change to a higher school, and
I think we were right in doing so. Eva feels happy at Croton,
there are nice children with her and she seems on the best of terms
with Mrs. Sch. and all the others. There are about as many Ame-
rican children as refugee children, Jews and Christians and that
mixed atmosphere seems to us a good and lively one. We did
not see her while we were in Newhaven as this terrible weather
and a series of colds, asthma and grippe from my part kept us
busy in Newhaven, but we phoned several times and had frequent
letters from Eva and detailed reports from Mrs. Sch. Had she
written them in English I would have sent them on to you as
it would have reassured you that Eva is with understanding people
who like her and who think in our lines. - Next week Eva
has her Easter holidays and I am taking her to New York to be
with us, and I am looking forward to have her with us for
a little while. If it is possible I shall go with her to see the
Smollett boys. I am going to have her photographed, take
her to a reliable dentist, maybe invite Robin Gilbert and
take them both to a show and try to make her at home in
hotel rooms. At least we have a little kitchenette and so we
can pretend home life to a certain degree by preparing
breakfast and occasionally eggs or sausages. - We returned
to New York two days ago and are glad to be back. Stefan
worked well in Newhaven and enjoyed the library facilities.
But as we had to stay in the Hotel and the weather was
most unpleasant we decided to leave rather suddenly,
and New York seems very attractive to us just now.
We got your brother's letter today. I am sorry that
he has not yet his visa and I hope the Consul will not be
too thorough in the examination of the affidavit value.
If it is not accepted we will have to try elsewhere. His ex-
tremely difficult now but he is one of the very few for whom one
can guarantee. On the whole I am glad that he is not sailing
just now, later in the summer the weather and the outlook will
be more sure, we suppose.
So please do not worry about Eva. She is developing
quite as she should, is as nice and lovable as ever, and in fighting
her tendencys for forgetting to write, Stefan has to overcome the combined
Mayer- and Altman heritage. Best love and kindest regards to all,
Lotte.
[vertical, left margin] release cable immediately
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Die Seite beginnt mit der Seitenzahl '3'. Am linken Rand befindet sich eine vertikale Notiz.
Rückseite des Dokuments, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (bleed-through). Leer.
